name: Question 11
problem: Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps $x\in {R}^{2}$ onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5$ of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
The spectral decomposition of a $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A$ is given by

$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =5.$ Computing $A-5I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{5}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11

Find the orthogonal projection matrix that maps x∈R2 onto the subspace spanned by an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue λ=5 of the matrix A=[1224].

a
15[1224]
b
[4221]
c
15[−4−1−12]
d
15[4221]
e
15[1224]
Submit

EXPLANATION

The spectral decomposition of a 2×2 symmetric matrix A is given by

A=λ1u1⋅u1T+λ2u2⋅u2T, where u1 and u2 are orthonormal eigenvectors of A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1 and λ2, respectively.

Moreover, ui⋅uiT is the projection matrix corresponding to ui.

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to λ=5. Computing A−5I, we get

A−5I=[1224]−5[1001]=[−422−1].

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

M=[−420210]R2:=R2+12R1∼[−420000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain x1=12x2. Hence, the general solution is

[12x2x2],x2∈R.

Therefore, setting x2=2, we get the eigenvector

v=[12],

where ‖v‖=5. Dividing v by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: u=v‖v‖=15[12]

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

u⋅uT=15[12]⋅15[12]=15[12]⋅[12]=15[1224].
